prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures $(3x + 10)°$ and the corresponding angle measures $(5x - 30)°$. What is the value of $x$?
hint: Corresponding angles formed by a transversal across parallel lines are equal.

hints.text: Corresponding angles formed by a transversal across parallel lines are equal.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try easier expressions: if corresponding angles are $(x + 20)°$ and $(2x)°$, then $x + 20 = 2x$ and $x = 20$. Congruent angles means set the expressions equal.

learningObjective: Set up an equation from an angle relationship in a parallel-line figure.
explanation: Corresponding angles are congruent when the lines are parallel, so set the expressions equal: $3x + 10 = 5x - 30$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Equal or supplementary decides the equation
steps: If the angles are congruent (corresponding, alternate interior, alternate exterior, vertical), set the expressions equal.
If they are supplementary (co-interior, or a linear pair), set the sum to $180$.
Identifying which relationship applies is the whole question — the algebra afterwards is routine.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Setting the sum to 180 — treating corresponding angles as supplementary — gives x = 25, a clean wrong answer.
Corresponding angles are CONGRUENT, so the expressions are set equal. Decide equal-or-supplementary from the angle relationship before writing the equation.
